memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart has two date dimensions, and choosing the wrong one silently changes the answer.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `transaction_date` for operational questions: daily sales, footfall, stock movement. It is when the transaction happened.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `fiscal_date` for anything compared against a budget or reported by period, because the fiscal year does not start in January.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: When a question says "last quarter" in a financial context it means a fiscal quarter, so group by `fiscal_date`.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Three metrics have "revenue" in the name and they are not interchangeable.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `metric_l1_total_net_revenue` by default. Net revenue is after returns and discounts.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_margin_bridge_gross_revenue` is gross, before returns and discounts. It exists for the margin bridge and is the wrong figure elsewhere.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_net_sales_summary_net_revenue` agrees with total net revenue but is scoped to its own SQL dataset's grain, so it does not slice by every dimension.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart's metrics are layered, and the layer is in both the metric id and its tags, L1 through L5.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L1 metrics (`metric_l1_*`) are base aggregations over a single fact column. They are the only layer that touches a fact directly.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L2 metrics (`metric_l2_cross_*`) are ratios between two L1 metrics, such as order count over net revenue.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L3 metrics (`metric_l3_*`) apply a filter to an L1 or L2 metric, usually a WHERE on a dimension attribute such as channel type.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L4 and L5 metrics compose further on top of the lower layers.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Prefer the lowest layer that answers the question. Total net revenue is an L1 metric; net revenue for one channel is an existing L3 metric, not an L1 metric with a filter added.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

metrics.description: Shows remaining (or overrun) capital budget by subtracting total spent amount from the total approved CapEx budget for the current selection (such as chosen filters and time period). Use it to monitor whether capital expenditure projects are under or over their approved budgets.
metrics.title: CapEx Budget Variance

metrics.description: Shows the total planned budget value by summing Budget Amount from the Budget Plan dataset, respecting any selected filters and breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total Budget Amount (Budget Plan)

metrics.description: Shows the total approved capital budget by summing the Approved Budget amounts across Capital Expenditure Projects for the current reporting scope (such as applied filters or time period). Use it to understand overall approved funding and compare totals across different project selections.
metrics.title: Total Approved Budget (Capital Expenditure Project)

metrics.description: Sums the Spent Amount from the Capital Expenditure Project dataset to show total capital project spend. Use it to monitor overall spending and compare spend across projects, time periods, or other business breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total Spent Amount (Capital Expenditure Project)

metrics.description: Shows total operating expenses (Operating Expenses (OpEx) by summing Operating Expenses (OpEx) from the Daily Profit & Loss data for the current reporting context, such as the selected date range, business unit, or other applied filters.
metrics.title: Total OpEx (Daily Profit & Loss)

metrics.description: Shows the total monetary value of intercompany (transactions between entities within the same organisation) recharges by summing the Recharge Amount from the Intercompany Recharge dataset for the current filters and selected time period.
metrics.title: Total Recharge Amount (Intercompany Recharge)

metrics.description: Shows the total value of operating expense transactions by summing the Amount from Operating Expense Transaction records for the current report filters and time period.
metrics.title: Total Amount (Operating Expense Transaction)

metrics.description: Shows total EBITDA by summing the EBITDA values from the Margin Bridge dataset for the current report or dashboard context. Use it to track overall operating profitability and compare results across the applied filters and breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total EBITDA (Margin Bridge)

metrics.description: Shows total gross margin by summing Gross Margin from the Margin Bridge dataset for the currently selected filters and time period. Use it to track overall profitability and support margin bridge analysis across business dimensions.
metrics.title: Total Gross Margin (Margin Bridge)

metrics.description: Shows total gross sales revenue by summing Gross Revenue from the Margin Bridge dataset, reflecting the current filters or reporting context in a report or dashboard. Useful as a baseline measure for revenue and margin bridge analysis.
metrics.title: Total Gross Revenue (Margin Bridge)

metrics.description: Totals Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) from the Daily Profit & Loss data to show overall direct costs for the currently selected period and any applied filters.
metrics.title: Total COGS

metrics.description: Totals the Revenue from the Daily Profit & Loss dataset to show net revenue for the current reporting scope, such as the selected time period and any applied filters.
metrics.title: Total Net Revenue

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) and Operating Expenses (OpEx) for the current reporting context in the Daily Profit & Loss data. Use it to understand whether direct costs or operating costs are driving spending changes over the selected period and filters.
metrics.title: COGS vs OpEx (Daily Profit & Loss) Change

metrics.description: Shows the variance between total operating expenses (Operating Expenses (OpEx) from the Daily Profit & Loss data and the total approved budget for Capital Expenditure Projects in the current reporting context (based on the selected time period and any applied filters). Use it to see whether Operating Expenses (OpEx) is above or below the approved capital budget and by how much.
metrics.title: OpEx (Daily Profit & Loss) vs Approved Budget (Capital Expenditure Project) Change

metrics.description: Shows the variance between the total approved budget for capital expenditure projects and the total amount spent, indicating how much budget remains or whether there is an overspend (if negative) for the current selection.
metrics.title: Approved Budget (Capital Expenditure Project) vs Spent Amount (Capital Expenditure Project) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between total capital expenditure project spend and total intercompany (transactions between entities within the same organisation) recharge amounts for the current filters and selected time period. Use it to assess whether project spending is running higher or lower than the recharges being applied.
metrics.title: Spent Amount (Capital Expenditure Project) vs Recharge Amount (Intercompany Recharge) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the variance between actual intercompany (transactions between entities within the same organisation) recharge amounts and the planned budget amount for the current filters and breakdowns. Use it to see whether recharge activity is over or under budget by subtracting total Budget Amount from total Recharge Amount.
metrics.title: Recharge Amount (Intercompany Recharge) vs Budget Amount (Budget Plan) Change

metrics.description: Shows the variance between the planned budget and actual gross revenue by subtracting Total Gross Revenue (Margin Bridge) from the Total Budget Amount (Budget Plan). Use it to quantify how much the budget is over or under gross revenue for the current filters and breakdowns.
metrics.title: Budget Amount (Budget Plan) vs Gross Revenue (Margin Bridge) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the absolute gap between Total Gross Revenue and Total Gross Margin in the Margin Bridge context (revenue minus margin). Use it to quantify how much revenue does not translate into margin for the current filters and time period.
metrics.title: Gross Revenue (Margin Bridge) vs Gross Margin (Margin Bridge) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the gap between Total Gross Margin and Total EBITDA in the Margin Bridge context. Use it to quantify how much gross margin exceeds (or falls short of) EBITDA and to see how that difference shifts across filters, time periods, and breakdowns.
metrics.title: Gross Margin (Margin Bridge) vs EBITDA (Margin Bridge) Change

sql.statement:
SELECT
    oh.order_date,
    SUM(ol.revenue) AS gross_revenue,
    SUM(ol.revenue) - SUM(COALESCE(cogs.cost, 0)) AS gross_margin,
    (SUM(ol.revenue) - SUM(COALESCE(cogs.cost, 0))) / NULLIF(SUM(ol.revenue), 0) AS gross_margin_pct,
    (SUM(ol.revenue) - SUM(COALESCE(cogs.cost, 0))) - SUM(COALESCE(opex.amount, 0)) AS ebitda
FROM {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_header oh
JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_line ol ON oh.order_id = ol.order_id
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_cogs_detail cogs ON ol.product_id = cogs.product_id
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_opex_transaction opex ON oh.order_date = opex.transaction_date
GROUP BY 1
